one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) Q3 2026 earnings. The date is unconfirmed: NEE IR lists no event yet, Oct 22 is a TipRanks estimate, and Q3 2025 was reported Oct 28, so late October is likely either way. NEE beat in both 2026 quarters (Q2 adj EPS $1.15, +9.5%) and targets the high end of $3.92-4.02. A small beat plus reaffirmed 8%+ / 9%+ growth is the expected outcome and mildly positive. (2) Virginia SCC local hearings on Oct 7 and 9, and a possible ruling on the AG's motion to treat the Sep 14 supplement as an amendment. That would move the statutory deadline from Jan 11 2027 into March: a timing negative, not a deal-killer. The SCC page (updated Sep 22) shows no ruling yet. (3) Rates: the 10-year hit 5.24% on Sep 28. After the cooler Aug PCE on Sep 30, October hike odds fell to ~36%, but the Sep 30 close already reflects that relief. The Oct 28 FOMC falls in the window and is two-sided. (4) New tail headline: the Sep 29 Oklahoma Uri liability ruling. Damages will be set at a trial with no date, so there is no likely cash effect in the window. The stock sits near its 52-week low after a 23% drawdown. I keep a small reversal/earnings lean (median ~$76.2) with ~6.3% monthly sigma, a little wider in the tails for the FOMC and the SCC ruling.

Blend ~$80.9, excluding ~$2.55 of dividends received over the year.

bear.story: The 10-year stays above 5.25% or rises further with an October/December hike. The Virginia review slips to March 2027 (the AG amendment motion is granted) and the concessions pile up. The market starts to price rejection or a burdensome condition, which would make NEE pay Dominion the $4.83B regulatory termination fee (~$2.30/share, DEFM14A). An Oklahoma Uri damages award adds headline risk (unquantified; $1B would be ~$0.50/share). The multiple falls to ~13x NTM EPS.

base.story: NEE delivers ~$4.01 in 2026 and reaffirms 8%+ (9%+ combined). The Virginia SCC approves with conditions in Jan-Mar 2027, NC/SC follow, and the close stays on track for 2H27. Rates stay high but stable. The stock holds ~17.5-18x NTM EPS of $4.58 and pays a ~3.4% yield on top.

bull.story: The 10-year falls back toward 4.3-4.6%. State approvals land early and the close comes ahead of schedule. FPL signs its first large-load data-center tariff deal and NEER backlog keeps compounding past 35 GW. The multiple recovers to ~21x NTM, still below the May peak.

thesis_break_reason: $62 is ~13.5x NTM EPS of $4.58 at the horizon (~14.6x today's NTM) and a ~4.2% forward yield, below the 2023 rate-shock trough. Rates alone take the multiple from ~22x to ~18x; they do not explain 13.5x. At $62 the market would be pricing a cut to the 8%+ / 6% dividend plan, forced block equity or a rating outlook change, a burdensome Virginia condition or rejection (with NEE owing the $4.83B fee), or a large Uri judgment. I keep $62 rather than moving lower: the break-fee cost (~$2.30/share) sits inside the bear case, not below the break.

reasoning: Round-2 revision. The supervisor's fact checks lead to five changes. (1) At the 2027-09-30 horizon the P/E should use NTM EPS of $4.58, not full-year 2028 ($4.67). (2) The dividend base is confirmed from the Jul 30 declaration: $0.6232/qtr, $2.49/yr, then 6% a year. (3) Under the DEFM14A, NEE pays the $4.83B regulatory fee, so a rejection costs ~$2.30/share. (4) The Oklahoma Uri liability ruling is a new tail. (5) October hike odds fell to ~36% after PCE. Q3 timing is unconfirmed. Valuation: P/E $81.5 (17.8x, flat to today's like-for-like ~17.9x NTM), forward-yield $80.5, and a down-weighted DDM $78.9, blended to $80.9 (from $83.5). Scenarios: bear $59 / 24% (break fee and Uri added), base $80 / 52%, bull $96 / 24%, mean ~$80.2. The ladder is a lognormal mixture with slightly fattened tails. P(>=76) is 0.595, down from 0.63 as the supervisor's revisit suggested, because my own fair value fell ~$2.6 and the bear case now carries a cash cost. I still sit a bit above a symmetric spread because the stock trades at ~17.9x NTM with fundamentals intact and a 3.4% yield near its 52-week low. Where I differ from the supervisor: I hold the thesis break at $62, not $61. Research was limited to three verification fetches (dividend release, Insurance Journal, SCC page). The Bloomberg PCE odds come from the supervisor and were not re-read.
